chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of this variant
predictions: The variant has no material TF-mediated effect on colorectal cancer; any association could reflect linkage or another mechanism.
Isogenic T-to-C editing will not produce a reproducible TF-dependent change in enhancer output or target-gene expression.
falsified_if: Isogenic editing shows a reproducible allelic regulatory effect that depends on a TF at this site and alters a relevant target gene.

chains.title: TCF7L2 binding on C increases POU5F1B expression
chains.element: The variant lies in enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3858447; whether this element is active in HCT116 is unestablished.

links.claim: This hypothesis proposes that alt C binds TCF7L2 more strongly than ref T; TCF7L2 is prioritized over other candidates because it is occupied at the site and expressed in HCT116, but no allele-specific binding or QBiC-SELEX model/result is provided to support this direction.
The variant lies within pELS cCRE EH38E3858447, although the reported chromatin maxima do not establish HCT116-specific activity.

POU5F1B is a candidate, not a demonstrated target of this element; proximity and gene-level CRC evidence do not establish this variant-to-gene link, and no significant GTEx eQTL or CRC GWAS association is reported.
HCT116 is a candidate context because TCF7L2 occupancy and expression are reported there, but a variant-dependent effect in these cells is not shown.
If this chain raises POU5F1B in colorectal cells, it could promote cancer-associated phenotypes; the cited study does not connect those effects to this variant or TCF7L2.

predictions: Allele-specific TCF7L2 occupancy is higher on C than T in HCT116.
The C allele increases TCF7L2-dependent enhancer output and POU5F1B expression; reducing TCF7L2 activity removes the allelic difference.
falsified_if: Allele-specific assays show no greater TCF7L2 occupancy on C, or show greater occupancy on T.
A controlled allelic assay finds no TCF7L2-dependent difference in enhancer output or POU5F1B expression.

next_experiment: Run the paired T- and C-allele enhancer reporter in HCT116 with and without TCF7L2 depletion. It is the least costly proposed functional test of the top two chains: H1 predicts a C-dependent, TCF7L2-dependent increase in reporter output, whereas H0 predicts no such effect. A positive result would still require endogenous validation.
